content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired PD#123456 -> embed-encoder-v4 canary across us-west-2. Synthetic embeddings job failing, p95 spike and 500s observed on /v1/embeddings.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD#123456 triggered (severity: high). On-call: @Mia. Escalation policy: infra-sre -> eng-lead.

Mia: Acked PD#123456. I see synthetic job alerting from canary weight 10%. Are real customer errors reported?

Rohit: I’m watching logs. Started seeing 502/504s and a p95 jump from ~120ms to ~1.8s on canary pods. Stack traces show kvcache misses + a model IO timeout. No full region outage, but a handful of production requests hit the canary and error.

Ben: I'm rolling back any active canary jobs now. What was in this release?

Lia: Release included embed-encoder-v4 (quant path) + packing changes. QA passed but perf tests were lighter. Customer-facing: a small percentage of requests hitting the embeddings route may have timed out; product metrics show a bump in error-rate for customer cohort C.

Kai: From infra, can confirm canary nodes are at higher CPU and GPU mem pressure. KV cache eviction rates spiked around the time of the deploy.

Rohit: Quick mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout (deploy-bot) 2) drop canary weight to 0% or rollback to v3 3) enable fallback routing to embed-encoder-v3 for errors 4) scale canary replicas up temporarily if we need to gather logs.

deploy-bot: Rollout pause requested by Rohit. Pausing canary for release r-2029-04-12. Current canary weight: 10% -> setting to 0%.

Mia: Thanks. Rohit, please proceed with rollback if you think it's faster than debugging in prod. We should reduce customer impact ASAP.

Rohit: Rolling back canary to embed-encoder-v3 now. Command run: 
```
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/embed-encoder embed-encoder=embed-encoder-v3
# decreasing canary traffic in routing table
routectl set-weight embeddings-service 0 --version v4
```

Rohit: Rolling back. Observability: starting to route new requests to v3. Watching error rate.

pagerduty-bot: PD#123456 acknowledged by Mia (08:12 UTC). Auto-escalation suspended.

Mia: Any customer-facing mitigation notes? Lia, can we enable a temporary message or retry to reduce surface area?

Lia: We can enable retry-on-failure with exponential backoff at the proxy layer for embeddings for 5 minutes while rollback completes. I'll coordinate with frontend.

Ben: After rollback complete, I'll open a debug session to gather perf traces from v4 in the canary cluster. Please do not purge logs yet.

Rohit: Metrics are stabilizing: p95 trending back to ~140ms, 500s dropping. KV eviction subsided after routing change.

Kai: Added temporary autoscaling on embedding pods to avoid brittle memory pressure while we investigate.

Mia: Good. PD note: incident severity reduced to medium; keeping incident open until postmortem tasks assigned.

incident-bot: deploy-bot reported rollback success for r-2029-04-12 at 08:20 UTC. Canary weight now 0%.

Rohit: Confirming rollback success. Collecting traces from the failed canary pods: kernel logs, model runner logs, and quant path dumps.

Ben: Found suspicious spike in memcpy times in quantized kernel path under high batch sizes. Hypothesis: new kernel selection prefers a kernel that regresses on our sequence lengths. Will run isolated perf bench.

Lia: Customer impact estimate: ~0.4% of embedding requests experienced errors during the 8-minute window. Recommending outbound customers on cohort C be notified with a short note if SLAs impacted.

Mia: Assigning follow-ups: 
- Rohit: gather full logs + traces and link to incident PD#123456 (due EOD)
- Ben: perf bench and reproduce in staging (due 24h)
- Kai: confirm autoscale config and add guardrails to avoid quick kvcache evictions (due 48h)
- Lia: customer comms draft (due next 2 hours)

Rohit: I've attached a diagnostics link in the incident page (PD#123456) with logs and traces.

pagerduty-bot: PD#123456 status updated -> resolved by Mia at 08:31 UTC (temporary mitigation: rollback).

Mia: Closing the page but keeping the Slack thread open for follow-ups. Please add notes to the postmortem template and tag the release engineer.

Ben: Will include kernel selection matrix and perf diff in the postmortem.

Lia: Drafting customer note now. Will share for review.

Rohit: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule a short postmortem tomorrow and loop in model-onboarding for v4 tuning before any re-rollout.

Mia: Handing off to Rohit for next steps. If anything regresses, re-page on PD#123456. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging, leaving for oncall follow-up.
